name: mastodon
summary: [Mastodon](https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/) is a free, open-source social network server based on ActivityPub where users can follow friends and discover new ones..

env.name: LOCAL_DOMAIN
env.description: This is the unique identifier of your server in the network. It cannot be safely changed later.

env.name: ES_ENABLED
env.description: Enable or disable Elasticsearch (requires a separate ES instance)

env.name: SECRET_KEY_BASE
env.description: Browser session secret. Changing it will break all active browser sessions.

env.name: OTP_SECRET
env.description: MFA secret. Changing it after initial setup will break two-factor authentication.

env.name: VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY
env.description: Push notification private key. Changing it after initial setup will break push notifications.

env.name: VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY
env.description: Push notification public key. Changing it after initial setup will break push notifications.

env.name: SMTP_FROM_ADDRESS
env.description: From address for emails send from Mastodon

env.name: S3_ENABLED
env.description: Enable or disable S3 storage of uploaded files

env.name: WEB_DOMAIN
env.description: This can be set if you want your server identifier to be different to the subdomain hosting Mastodon. See [https://docs.joinmastodon.org/admin/config/#basic](https://docs.joinmastodon.org/admin/config/#basic)

env.name: S3_ALIAS_HOST
env.description: Alternate hostname for object fetching if you are front the S3 connections.

env.name: SIDEKIQ_ONLY
env.description: Only run the sidekiq service in this container instance. For large scale instances that need better queue handling.

env.name: SIDEKIQ_QUEUE
env.description: The name of the sidekiq queue to run in this container. See [notes](https://docs.joinmastodon.org/admin/scaling/#sidekiq-queues).

env.name: SIDEKIQ_DEFAULT
env.description: Set to `true` on the main container if you're running additional sidekiq instances. It will run the `default` queue.

env.name: SIDEKIQ_THREADS
env.description: The number of threads for sidekiq to use. See [notes](https://docs.joinmastodon.org/admin/scaling/#sidekiq-threads).

env.name: DB_POOL
env.description: The size of the DB connection pool, must be *at least* the same as `SIDEKIQ_THREADS`. See [notes](https://docs.joinmastodon.org/admin/scaling/#sidekiq-threads).

env.name: NO_CHOWN
env.description: Set to `true` to skip chown of /config on init. *READ THE APPLICATION NOTES BEFORE SETTING THIS*.

env.name: MASTODON_PROMETHEUS_EXPORTER_ENABLED
env.description: If set to `true`, Mastodon’s Ruby processes (web & Sidekiq) will enable the Prometheus instrumentation.

docs.setup:
We provide aliases for the common commands that execute in the correct context so that environment variables from secrets are available to them:

* To generate keys for `SECRET_KEY_BASE` & `OTP_SECRET` run `docker run --rm -it --entrypoint /bin/bash lscr.io/linuxserver/mastodon:latest generate-secret` once for each.

* To generate keys for `VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY` & `VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY` run `docker run --rm -it --entrypoint /bin/bash lscr.io/linuxserver/mastodon:latest generate-vapid`

* To generate keys for `ACTIVE_RECORD_ENCRYPTION_DETERMINISTIC_KEY`, `ACTIVE_RECORD_ENCRYPTION_KEY_DERIVATION_SALT`, & `ACTIVE_RECORD_ENCRYPTION_PRIMARY_KEY` run `docker run --rm -it --entrypoint /bin/bash lscr.io/linuxserver/mastodon:latest generate-active-record`

Both of the secret generation aliases above can be run without any other setup having been carried out.

* To use `tootctl` you can run something like `docker exec -it lscr.io/linuxserver/mastodon /tootctl <command>`

Using `tootctl` requires you to complete the initial Mastodon configuration first.

This container *requires* separate postgres and redis instances to run.

We support all of the official [environment variables](https://docs.joinmastodon.org/admin/config) for configuration. In place of adding them all to your run/compose you can use an env file such as [this example](https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/blob/main/.env.production.sample) from the upstream project.

For more information check out the [mastodon documentation](https://docs.joinmastodon.org/).

### Running separate sidekiq instances

It is currently only supported to run a single queue per container instance *or* all queues in a single container instance.

All containers must share the same `/config` mount and be on a common docker network.

### NO_CHOWN Option

On larger Mastodon instances, our init process to verify that permissions are set correctly can noticeably slow down the container startup. If you are experiencing this, you can set `NO_CHOWN` to `true` to skip that step of the init.

*Do NOT set this on first run of the container. If you enable this option you are taking full responsibility for ensuring that the permissions in your /config mount are correct. If you're even slightly unsure, don't set it.*

### Strict reverse proxies

This image automatically redirects to https with a self-signed certificate. If you are using a reverse proxy which validates certificates, you need to [disable this check for the container](https://docs.linuxserver.io/faq#strict-proxy).

changelog.text: Rebase to Alpine 3.21, replace deprecated imagemagick with vips.
Rebase to Alpine 3.20, enable [Active Record Encryption](https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/pull/29831/files). Existing users should update their nginx confs to avoid http2 deprecation warnings.
Rebase to Alpine 3.18, migrate to s6v3.
Updated nginx conf to fix bring inline with Mastodon configuration (fixes Elk integration).
